limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

G1; Missing period; MATERIAL; Financial foundation; Liquidity; Fundamental credit; No source is dated after 2026-08-07. Third quarter 2026 results and any financing, acquisition or rating event between 2026-08-08 and 2026-11-05 are not in the file set; debt, cash, liquidity and covenant leverage are as of June 30, 2026, 128 days before the as-of date. The third quarter 2025 report was signed on November 5, 2025, so the 2026 report may fall at or after the cutoff.; Research question: locate any report, release or current report dated after 2026-08-07 and up to the cutoff.

G2; Missing document; MATERIAL; Business & governance; Part III of the annual report is incorporated from a proxy statement that is not supplied: board composition, independence, executive pay and the beneficial ownership table are not established.; Supply the 2026 proxy statement.

G3; Conflict: definition; MATERIAL; Financial foundation; Fundamental credit; Covenant capacity; Issuer-reported credit agreement leverage is 3.2x (3.1x netting all cash) for Q2 2026, while total debt over four-quarter adjusted EBITDA is 3.63x (3.45x net) on the same debt. The lenders' EBITDA, its add-backs and the cash netting rule are not supplied, so neither figure is chosen and the difference is not reconciled.; Carry both figures with their definitions; supply the compliance certificate or credit agreement.

G4; Missing document; MINOR; Legal & covenants; Covenant capacity; Structural priority; The ABL credit agreement with five amendments, the three note indentures and the list of subsidiaries are not supplied. Covenant levels (interest coverage 2.5x, Leverage Ratio 5.25x, Secured Leverage Ratio 3.25x) were last printed for FY2025 and the second quarter 2026 report does not restate them; no reported interest coverage or secured leverage figure is printed in any of the seven files.; Supply executed documents and the latest compliance certificate.

G5; Missing evidence; MINOR; Ratings & triggers; Ratings, outlooks and agencies are not stated (searched 'Moody', 'S&P', 'Fitch', 'rating', 'downgrade' and 'outlook' in all seven files); only the existence of ratings, a fall-away covenant and the investment-grade status of customers are printed.; Supply agency reports or run a research question.

G6; Missing detail; MINOR; Refinancing & LME; Structural priority; The month and day of maturity of the 2031, 2033 and 2035 notes and the names of the guarantor subsidiaries are not printed; the filings give the maturity year, the call dates and a guarantee on a senior unsecured basis by the Company and certain unnamed subsidiaries.; Supply the indentures or the exhibit list of guarantors.

G7; Missing detail; MINOR; Liquidity; ABL availability is printed only as USD 1.6 billion; the borrowing base amount and any availability block are not printed, and the commitment-based ceiling is 1,604,483 thousand.; Supply the latest borrowing base certificate.

G8; Conflict: presentation; MINOR; Financial foundation; Earnings changes; Filings and releases before the second quarter 2026 report use two segments (Contract Services and Other Services); the second quarter report recasts prior periods into three. The issuer states the recast changes no consolidated result; first quarter 2026 Compression Infrastructure revenue of 306,985 equals the earlier Contract Services figure, but 17,985 thousand of first quarter growth capital expenditure moves from Compression Infrastructure to Power Infrastructure.; Use the recast figures from the second quarter 2026 release for comparisons.

G9; Preliminary figure; MINOR; Financial foundation; The DPS purchase price allocation, including goodwill of 344,782 thousand, is preliminary and may change within one year of closing.; Check later filings for the final allocation.

G10; Missing detail; MINOR; Liquidity; Forward credit model; Purchase commitments of USD 2.5 billion are not split between compression units and power generation units, and the timing of down payments under the one-gigawatt turbine order is not itemized; only about USD 244.8 million of power generation asset commitments entered into after March 31, 2026 is separately stated.; Carry the printed twelve-month amount of USD 587.9 million and flag the rest as unspecified.

G11; Contingency; MINOR; Business & governance; Fundamental credit; The Department of Justice, OFAC and SEC matter on Mexican payments has no estimate of loss or penalty; the issuer does not expect a significant adverse impact but gives no assurance.; Monitor; no amount can be set from the sources.

G12; Definition; MINOR; Financial foundation; The Texas sales and use tax liability of USD 65.8 million is the Texas portion only, while the accrued liabilities line for sales tax is 69,635 thousand; the gap between them is not explained.; Use the Texas figure for the contingency and the accrued line for the balance sheet, each labelled.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Financing moved in several steps. In September 2025 the company issued USD 1.2 billion of senior unsecured notes due 2033 and 2035, topped up by USD 200.0 million, and amended its asset-based facility to USD 2.0 billion with a September 2030 maturity. On March 20, 2026 it issued USD 1.0 billion of senior unsecured notes due 2031 and redeemed the 7.25% notes due 2029 on April 10, 2026 at a premium that cost USD 27.2 million. On May 13, 2026 it sold shares in an offering that closed on May 15, 2026 for net proceeds of USD 836.1 million, and on April 2, 2026 it amended the asset-based facility again to change how leverage is calculated. facts.text: - The compression franchise is the credit anchor, and it is contracted: customers pay a fixed monthly fee, utilization is 98.2%, the adjusted gross margin is 70.0%, and customers supply the fuel gas and reimburse property taxes, so little revenue leaks before it reaches cash flow. facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: The first weakness is negative free cash flow from the power build-out. facts.label: Business profile and credit linkage
facts.text: Compression customers pay a fixed monthly fee, billed ahead of the service month and generally due within 30 days, for primary terms of one to seven years, or three to five years for large units, and most contracts carry an annual inflation adjustment. Compression was 84.4% of first-half 2026 revenue, power 4.5% and other services 11.1%. The structure resembles midstream take-or-pay: revenue depends on units staying under contract, not on gas volumes, which makes cash flow visible and sticky but ties it to renewals and to one product in one region. For creditors the model supports debt service and liquidity through each contract term, while refinancing confidence depends on how much of the fleet rolls onto new terms at similar rates and on whether the new power business earns what the capital spent on it requires. facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Compression revenue rose 7.4% in the second quarter of 2026 on 2.7% more revenue-generating horsepower and 4.1% more output per unit, with 5.3% fewer units, so growth comes from larger units placed under contract and has to be bought with growth capital. facts.text: The downside begins with a sustained fall in oil and gas prices that slows drilling and completions in the Permian Basin and Eagle Ford Shale, where 82.8% of compression assets sit. The first operational break is at renewal: units that have reached the end of their primary terms, 9.0% of horsepower at the end of 2025, can leave on 30 to 90 days' notice, and the contracted book thins quickly after 2027, so a loss of 10% of compression revenue is the illustrative size used here, about the whole month-to-month group and a little more. At the 70.0% adjusted gross margin the loss removes USD 85.5 million of EBITDA, so four-quarter adjusted EBITDA falls to USD 680.6 million and reported EBITDA to USD 517.9 million; total debt becomes 4.00x adjusted EBITDA and 5.26x reported EBITDA, and net debt 3.80x and 5.00x, while adjusted EBITDA still covers cash interest 3.68x and reported EBITDA 2.80x. If costs did not fall at all, the loss would be USD 122.1 million and total debt would be 4.23x adjusted and 5.66x reported EBITDA. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Kodiak presents an adequate business profile supported by contracted, high-margin compression cash flows and a customer base of investment-grade names, but credit quality is constrained by negative free cash flow from a debt-assisted power build-out, leverage of 4.52x reported EBITDA and a financial policy that keeps paying out without a sponsor. Cash-flow durability appears adequate for compression and not fully assessable for power, which has one quarter of history. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on continued access to equity and notes markets, revolver availability, and renewals of the compression book from 2027 to 2029, with no maturity before 2030. The primary downside path is a fall in Permian demand that ends month-to-month units while power capital is already committed. Further analysis would require the lenders' covenant definitions, the proxy statement, power contract terms, the third-quarter results and current market prices. Top risk: debt-assisted power growth ahead of signed long contracts. ## Findings
### Bottom line

Kodiak's seven supplied filings and releases are enough to start a credit snapshot through the quarter ended June 30, 2026, but without executed credit documents, ratings or as-of-date market prices creditors cannot test covenant mechanics, guarantor coverage or priority of claims.

The debt stack, liquidity, leases, purchase commitments and contingencies are all printed with locators, so financial foundation, business and fundamental credit work can proceed on that basis. Two limits cap how far any conclusion can be pushed: no source is dated after August 7, 2026, leaving the latest balance sheet 128 days old at the as-of date, and the lenders' EBITDA definition behind the reported 3.2x covenant leverage is not supplied, so that ratio cannot be recomputed. Governance depth is also limited because the proxy statement is missing.

## Findings
### Bottom line

At June 30, 2026 total debt is 4.52x reported EBITDA and 3.56x issuer-adjusted EBITDA, so creditors should underwrite the higher reported figure until the lenders' covenant definition is supplied, because the gap between the two is add-backs the issuer chooses.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20; 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 56; calculation C05; calculation C06; calculation C15

Near-term liquidity is adequate: cash and undrawn ABL commitments of about USD 1.6 billion face no material maturity until 2030. Free cash flow was negative in the second quarter of 2026 as growth spending on power generation rose, and the share issue raised more than the cash paid for the acquisition, so net debt rose only slightly over the half-year. The covenant leverage the company reports, 3.2x, cannot be recomputed from the filings, and four-quarter earnings carry one quarter of the acquired business against its full financing.

- Nothing dated after August 7, 2026 was supplied, so debt, cash, liquidity and the four-quarter figures stop at June 30, 2026, 128 days before the as-of date; severity High; the third quarter 2026 report would close it.

- The lenders' EBITDA, add-backs and cash netting used for the reported covenant leverage of 3.2x are not supplied, so that ratio cannot be recomputed and the calculated 4.52x and 3.56x are not comparable with it; severity High; the compliance certificate would close it.

- The borrowing base amount is not printed, so undrawn commitments of 1,604.483 are a ceiling, not confirmed availability, and the December 31, 2024 commitment is not in the supplied files, so the first undrawn figure is not supplied; severity Medium; the borrowing base certificate and the 2024 filing would close it.

- Carrying value by debt instrument is not disclosed; only the total and the aggregate premium and issuance cost are, so each instrument carries its principal and one financing cost adjustment row reconciles to total debt; severity Low; it would close only if the issuer discloses carrying value by instrument.

- Other borrowings of 4,283 thousand have no stated security, ranking, rate or maturity beyond the 2026 and 2027 amounts, and finance leases have no stated rank, so both are left out of the debt stack; severity Low; the equipment financing agreements would close it.

- The exact maturity month and day of the 2031, 2033 and 2035 notes and the names of the guarantor subsidiaries are not printed, only the maturity year and a guarantee by the Company and certain subsidiaries; severity Medium; the indentures would close it.

- The acquired power business contributes one quarter of earnings to the four-quarter figures but all of its financing to debt, and the issuer gives no pro forma four-quarter EBITDA, so 2026 leverage overstates run-rate leverage by an amount that is not established; severity Medium; a pro forma figure from a later filing would close it.
- The acquisition's purchase price allocation is preliminary and goodwill of 344,782 thousand may change; severity Low; later filings would close it.

- The power segment has no value before April 2026, and the impairment, extinguishment and derivative lines print no value in some periods, so each such cell is not supplied rather than zero; severity Low; no action is needed beyond reading the recast figures.

- Gross profit, interest income and cash tax by line are not statement lines: cost of operations excludes depreciation and amortization, interest income sits within other income and expense, and cash taxes paid are in the supplemental disclosure; severity Low; no figure is invented.

- The Texas sales and use tax liability and the Mexico payments matter are contingencies that this module records only as items inside other expense and adjusted EBITDA; no loss estimate exists for the Mexico matter; severity Medium; later filings would close it.

- Purchase commitments of USD 2.5 billion are not split between compression and power equipment, which limits any view of future capital calls beyond the twelve-month amount; severity Medium; later disclosure would close it.

spans.text: ## Request

Business and governance fact pack for Kodiak Gas Services, Inc. (kgs), as of 2026-11-05, under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: business and operating model, ownership and control, transactions, governance and financial-policy behaviour, taken from the seven supplied issuer files.
## Sources

| EX-99.1_2026-05-11_kgsq12026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl | Earnings release (Exhibit 99.1) for the first quarter of 2026 | 2026-05-11 | 28d16a69c5b1c7a653a4d372cd4408de628fa59c0bf8c9e28886ae87b3878e62 | Management description of the power business and the purchase-leaseback of compression units. |

| EX-99.1_2026-08-06_kgsq22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl | Earnings release (Exhibit 99.1) for the second quarter of 2026 | 2026-08-06 | 1fc26851224dc87b9b00439921419ff667a90cf4a5077539afcc9f2e07b9ff72 | Management description of the second quarter, power fleet statistics and the July 2026 lease buyout. |

No external sources were used. The run settings hold dates and blank inputs and are not listed as evidence.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Kodiak's sponsor has fully sold out and its fixed-fee compression contracts carry USD 2.6 billion of remaining revenue, so creditors now rely on management's financial policy, which funds both shareholder payouts and a large move into power generation.

Contract terms, investment-grade customers and a utilization rate of 98.2% support the compression cash flows, but the power business has one quarter of history and its leases sit outside the remaining-revenue figure. Shareholder payouts of USD 263.5 million in 2025 exceeded issuer-defined free cash flow of USD 229.6 million, and the executed credit documents that would show how much further the company may distribute were not supplied.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 61; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_kgsq22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_kgs-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 77–78; 10-K_2025-12-31_kgs-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-K_2025-12-31_kgs-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 128; calculation C01
### Key findings

- The compression business is the credit anchor: customers pay a fixed monthly fee under terms of one to seven years, only 9.0% of revenue-generating horsepower is on month-to-month terms, and remaining contract revenue grew from USD 1.6 billion at the end of 2025 to USD 2.6 billion at June 30, 2026. Contract revenue visibility for compression is therefore multi-year, although it excludes the power leases.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kgs-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_kgs-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 117; 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 17; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_kgsq22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 6

- Concentration is the main business risk: the four largest customers, all investment-grade, supplied about 30% of revenue in the first half of 2026, and 82.8% of compression assets sit in the Permian Basin and Eagle Ford Shale, so a regional drilling downturn or the loss of one large customer would hit utilization of 98.2% with little idle fleet to cushion it.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kgs-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_kgs-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 61; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_kgsq22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 6

- The power acquisition changes the business model more than the balance sheet: the purchase of Distributed Power Solutions closed on April 1, 2026 for consideration of USD 726.4 million, power revenue was USD 32.9 million in the second quarter, 8.4% of revenue, and the one disclosed lease has an initial term ending April 1, 2028. Power revenue is lease-based, runs from short-term to multi-year and sits outside the remaining-revenue figure, while purchase commitments of USD 2.5 billion include a multi-year Baker Hughes power generation arrangement and the company announced a one-gigawatt turbine order for delivery by 2030, so the build-out has to be financed before it earns.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 37; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_kgsq22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_kgsq22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation C04

- The sponsor is gone, which removes sponsor extraction and sponsor support at the same time: the EQT AB affiliates held about 43.1% at the start of 2025 and nothing from December 2, 2025, and the company itself bought back USD 93.3 million of its shares from them during 2025. Who now controls the company is not established: the supplied files name no holder, and the proxy statement was not supplied.

- Financial policy returns cash and still grows: 2025 dividends of USD 159.6 million plus repurchases of USD 104.0 million came to USD 263.5 million against issuer-defined free cash flow of USD 229.6 million, though discretionary cash flow of USD 461.7 million covered them. In 2026 the company paid USD 92.6 million of dividends in the first half and raised USD 836.1 million of equity in May 2026, more than the cash paid for the acquisition, which limited the rise in debt, while the remaining repurchase authorization of USD 31.7 million at the end of 2025 expires on December 31, 2026.

- Governance and compliance disclosure is adequate for monitoring but incomplete: the annual statements carry an unqualified audit opinion and effective internal control, related-party service costs are small, and a voluntary self-report of payments by the sold Mexican business to the Department of Justice, OFAC and the SEC has no stated amount, alongside a Texas sales tax liability of USD 65.8 million. The unquantified investigation and the missing board, pay and ownership detail limit how far governance can be rated.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a lower-risk view is that payouts were covered by discretionary cash flow, the share issue raised more than the cash price of the acquisition, the 2029 notes were replaced by 2031 notes at a lower coupon with no collateral release, priming or exchange, and the customers are investment-grade. That evidence would win if the third quarter 2026 report shows free cash flow recovering as power capital spending is delivered and no new debt-funded distribution or acquisition.

The view would move the other way if the company authorizes a larger repurchase program, funds power growth with the credit facility rather than equity or cash flow, signs power contracts materially shorter than its build-out financing, or discloses a loss from the Mexican matter; any one of these would change the sponsor-and-governance read from mixed to adverse.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 30; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_kgsq22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 6
### Limitations

- The proxy statement was not supplied, so board composition, independence, pay and holder sizes are not established, which limits the ownership and control conclusion to the sponsor exit and does not support a view on who now controls the company.

- The executed credit agreement and indentures were not supplied, so the capacity to pay dividends, repurchase shares or invest is not measured, which keeps the financial-policy conclusion to observed behaviour rather than permitted behaviour.
- Nothing dated after August 7, 2026 was supplied, so the capital-allocation read may be stale for the third quarter and any later dividend, repurchase or financing.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 66
- The power business has one quarter of reported history and its lease revenue is excluded from remaining contract revenue, which means the durability conclusion applies to compression only.

- No investor presentation or management discussion beyond the filings and releases was supplied, so management's description of strategy is read only as issuer language, which weakens any view of growth targets beyond the disclosed guidance.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-05-11_kgsq12026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_kgsq22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The power acquisition is the transaction that matters most for creditors. Kodiak agreed on February 5, 2026 to buy Distributed Power Solutions in an equity and cash deal valued at about USD 675.0 million at signing, and closed on April 1, 2026 with consideration of USD 726.4 million, made up of cash of USD 587.3 million and 2.4 million shares worth USD 139.0 million at the closing price; the purchase price allocation is preliminary and goodwill of USD 344.8 million may change. The agreement carried a termination fee of USD 37.1 million payable by Kodiak under certain circumstances.

Financing moved in several steps. In September 2025 the company issued USD 1.2 billion of senior unsecured notes due 2033 and 2035, topped up by USD 200.0 million, and amended its asset-based facility to USD 2.0 billion with a September 2030 maturity. On March 20, 2026 it issued USD 1.0 billion of senior unsecured notes due 2031 and redeemed the 7.25% notes due 2029 on April 10, 2026 at a premium that cost USD 27.2 million. On May 13, 2026 it sold shares in an offering that closed on May 15, 2026 for net proceeds of USD 836.1 million, and on April 2, 2026 it amended the asset-based facility again to change how leverage is calculated.

Events after the quarter are dated and kept out of the June 30, 2026 position: in July 2026 the company bought out leased compression equipment of about 43,000 horsepower for about USD 32.8 million, and on August 5, 2026 it declared a dividend of USD 0.49 per share payable on August 27, 2026.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Kodiak's contracted compression business covers its interest and faces no material maturity before 2030, but the power build-out is cash-negative and is funded first by equity and then by debt, so creditors should expect leverage to hold near today's level, not fall.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-08-06_kgsq22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 49; calculation C05; calculation C07

Net debt was 4.29x reported EBITDA at June 30, 2026; pro forma net leverage is 4.34x after the July 2026 lease buyout and 4.37x after the dividend payable on August 27, 2026, each taken on its own. Liquidity of about USD 1.7 billion makes a near-term payment problem unlikely, and remaining contract revenue of USD 2.6 billion covers 85.67% to 89.76% of guided second-half compression revenue but only 59.46% to 60.89% of a flat 2027, so renewals from 2027 are the real test.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 17; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_kgsq22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 5; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_kgsq22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C02; calculation C19; calculation C21
### Key findings

- The compression franchise is the credit anchor, and it is contracted: customers pay a fixed monthly fee, utilization is 98.2%, the adjusted gross margin is 70.0%, and customers supply the fuel gas and reimburse property taxes, so little revenue leaks before it reaches cash flow. Contracted visibility lengthened sharply in 2026, with revenue due after 2026 rising to 2.74x its December 2025 level, which shows customers committing for longer, although the filings do not split new units from renewals.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kgs-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_kgs-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 116; 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 17; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_kgsq22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_kgsq22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation C03

- Leverage stays near current levels in 2026 on the issuer's own guidance. Total debt is 4.52x reported EBITDA and 3.56x adjusted EBITDA, guidance implies free cash flow after growth spending short by USD 125 million to USD 235 million, dividends of about USD 191.7 million add to it, and the second half needs USD 173.5 million to USD 283.5 million against cash of USD 137.6 million at June 30, 2026 (pro forma cash is not established). On guided adjusted EBITDA of USD 830 million to USD 860 million this is an indication, not a pro forma, of year-end net leverage of 3.25x to 3.50x adjusted, against 3.38x at June 30, 2026; Financial foundation states pro forma net leverage only on reported EBITDA, so the adjusted pro forma is not established.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-08-06_kgsq22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C04; calculation C05; calculation C06; calculation C07

- Liquidity and the maturity profile remove refinancing risk for several years: cash and undrawn revolver commitments of about USD 1.7 billion face only USD 4.3 million of equipment financing before the revolver matures in September 2030, 86.17% of principal is fixed-rate notes due 2031 to 2035, and the issuer estimates that a 1.0% rise in rates would add only USD 3.1 million of interest on the revolver before swaps. The constraint to watch is revolver availability, because the lockbox and the test for revolver-funded dividends both key off USD 100.0 million of availability.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 60; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_kgsq22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C12; calculation C21

- Covenant headroom looks wide on the issuer's reported figures and cannot be tested independently. The credit agreement leverage ratio was reported at 3.2x against a maximum of 5.25x printed in the annual report, an interest cover minimum of 2.5x compares with 3.26x on the weakest measure computed here, and the only secured instrument is the drawn revolver at 0.63x reported EBITDA against a 3.25x secured maximum, with no step-down printed. The lenders' EBITDA, the cash netting allowance and the 2026 amendment change the calculation, so headroom in EBITDA terms is not calculable.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kgs-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 72; 10-K_2025-12-31_kgs-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 121; 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 21; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_kgsq22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 5; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C14

- Financial policy is the main judgement after the sponsor exit: payouts of USD 263.5 million in 2025 were 114.79% of issuer-defined free cash flow, yet discretionary cash flow covered dividends 2.89x, the quarterly dividend is USD 0.49 per share, and USD 31.7 million of repurchase authority remains until December 31, 2026. Management states that it expects to fund dividends and growth from discretionary cash flow and, if that falls short, to use the revolver or cut growth spending, which makes growth spending the first lever for creditors.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kgs-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 77; 10-K_2025-12-31_kgs-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 48; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C11; calculation C17

- The power business is the least proven part of the credit: it contributed USD 32.9 million of revenue in its first quarter, 8.41% of the total, and its leases sit outside remaining contract revenue. Power growth spending of USD 400 million to USD 450 million in 2026 is 3.20x to 4.74x the revenue guided for the year, and since the February 2026 guidance, which excluded the acquisition, guided growth and other capital spending has risen by USD 450 million to USD 490 million while the midpoint of adjusted EBITDA guidance rose USD 80 million, turning an implied free cash flow surplus of USD 165 million to USD 235 million into the shortfall. In May 2026 management described its customer discussions for the ordered capacity as advanced rather than concluded, so equipment is being paid for before long contracts are shown.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 18; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_kgsq22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 5; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_kgsq22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 7; EX-99.1_2026-05-11_kgsq12026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-05-11_kgsq12026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-02-25_kgsq42025earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; calculation C16; calculation C25

- Cash conversion weakened in the first half of 2026 for reasons that have not yet reversed: operating cash flow fell by USD 120.9 million to USD 170.6 million as working capital absorbed USD 154.6 million, mainly receivables and accrued liabilities, so operating cash flow was 41.93% of adjusted EBITDA against 83.88% in 2025. If collections do not catch up, the second-half cash call above is too small.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 49; calculation C09; calculation C10

- Demand risk sits in few customers and one region but is cushioned by credit quality: the four largest customers, all investment-grade, were about 30% of first-half revenue, 82.8% of compression assets are in the Permian Basin and Eagle Ford Shale, and 9.0% of revenue-generating horsepower was month-to-month at year-end, terminable on 30 to 90 days' notice.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kgs-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_kgs-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_kgs-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 61; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Claims outside the debt figure are modest except for purchase commitments: leases are 3.54% of carrying debt, purchase commitments are USD 2.5 billion of which USD 587.9 million falls due within twelve months, and a Texas sales tax liability of USD 65.8 million and an unquantified Mexico payments matter remain open. No pension, retiree medical, factoring or supply-chain finance obligation appears in any supplied filing or release.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 48; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C18
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that the first half of 2026 absorbed an acquisition of USD 576.0 million and capital spending of USD 318.6 million while net debt rose only USD 35.3 million, because the USD 836.1 million equity issue paid for most of it, and that guided adjusted EBITDA for 2026 was raised while quarterly adjusted EBITDA rose 21.7% from a year earlier. Revenue due after 2026 also grew 2.74x in six months, and the company says it can cut growth spending or lean on the revolver if cash flow disappoints. That evidence would win if the third and fourth quarters show receivables reversing, free cash flow at the better end of guidance and signed multi-year power contracts, in which case year-end leverage would fall below 3.25x.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 49; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_kgsq22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_kgsq22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 5; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_kgsq22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C03; calculation C06; calculation C08

The view would move against creditors if second-half cash flow needs more than USD 283.5 million, if the board adds a new repurchase program or raises the dividend while free cash flow is negative, if power capacity is delivered without long contracts, or if renewals of compression units reaching the end of their primary terms in 2027 and 2028 come in at lower rates; any one would push net leverage on the adjusted measure toward or above 3.50x, and the equity cushion of 2.77x net debt at the May 2026 offering price would then be the main protection, although it is not a current value.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kgs-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 26; EX-99.1_2026-05-11_kgsq12026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C02; calculation C06; calculation C07; calculation C13
### Limitations

- The lenders' EBITDA definition, compliance certificate and borrowing base are not supplied, so the covenant conclusion rests on the issuer's reported 3.2x and the maximum printed in the annual report, and headroom cannot be sized in EBITDA terms.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kgs-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 72; 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 21; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_kgsq22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 5

- The latest reported results are for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, so the indicated year-end net leverage of 3.25x to 3.50x rests on guidance issued on August 6, 2026 and on an assumed fourth-quarter dividend, and it changes if the third quarter or later events moved debt or guidance.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-08-06_kgsq22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 29; calculation C06; calculation C07

- Only one power lease is described and the purchase price allocation is preliminary, so the view that power spending runs ahead of earnings treats power as unproven, and it would soften if long contracts at the reported margin were shown.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 18; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_kgsq22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 6

- No current market prices, bond spreads or ratings are supplied, so market access is judged from the issues completed in 2025 and 2026 and the equity cushion rests on a May 2026 offering price that is not a current value.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-08-06_kgsq22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 22; calculation C13

- No peer data is supplied, so the comparison with other leveraged issuers in contract compression and power is qualitative, and the Average assessments of scale and competitive position could be too high or too low.
### Strengths and weaknesses

The first strength is fixed-fee compression contracts with investment-grade customers. Remaining contract revenue of USD 2.6 billion, utilization of 98.2% and an adjusted gross margin of 70.0% mean most compression cash flow is set by contract rather than by volumes, and customers bear fuel and property tax costs, so cash reaches debt service with little leakage. For creditors this supports debt service on the existing fleet through a downturn of moderate length.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kgs-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_kgs-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 17; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_kgsq22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 6

The second strength is liquidity with a distant maturity wall. Cash and undrawn revolver commitments of about USD 1.7 billion face no material maturity until the revolver falls due in September 2030, and 86.17% of principal is fixed-rate notes due from 2031. That removes refinancing from the near-term default path and leaves time to adjust growth spending.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-08-06_kgsq22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C12; calculation C21

The third strength is proven access to both debt and equity markets. The company issued USD 1.0 billion of 2031 notes in March 2026, raised USD 836.1 million of equity in May 2026 and, in the first half, paid for an acquisition of USD 576.0 million while net debt rose only USD 35.3 million. Equity funding of growth limits leverage drift and shows that investors were willing to finance the plan.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 22; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_kgsq22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C08

The fourth strength is pricing support from tight equipment supply in large-horsepower compression. Utilization rose to 98.2% from 97.2% a year earlier and the adjusted gross margin to 70.0% from 68.3%, and management describes long lead times for new large units. Tight supply slows competing fleet additions and supports renewals as contracts reach the end of their primary terms from 2027.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-08-06_kgsq22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_kgsq22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 6; EX-99.1_2026-05-11_kgsq12026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 3

The fifth strength is low maintenance capital need. Maintenance spending was USD 76.0 million in 2025, 10.63% of adjusted EBITDA, and guidance of USD 80 million to USD 90 million for 2026 is 9.30% to 10.84%, so nearly all other spending is growth that can be slowed. That is the main lever for protecting leverage in a downturn, although USD 2.5 billion of equipment orders limit how fast it can be used.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kgs-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 77; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_kgsq22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 29; calculation C11

The first weakness is negative free cash flow from the power build-out. Guided growth and other spending for 2026 exceeds guided discretionary cash flow by USD 125 million to USD 235 million, and issuer-defined free cash flow was negative USD 87.5 million in the second quarter of 2026. Because dividends continue, the gap is met from cash and then the revolver, so debt rises while power earnings are still ramping.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-08-06_kgsq22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 6; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_kgsq22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C05; calculation C06

The second weakness is a leverage level that depends on whose EBITDA is used. Total debt is 4.52x reported EBITDA and 3.56x issuer-adjusted EBITDA, add-backs were 21.60% of reported 2025 EBITDA, and the covenant ratio of 3.2x cannot be rebuilt from the filings. Creditors should underwrite the higher figure until the lenders' definition is shown.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-08-06_kgsq22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C20

The third weakness is financial policy without a sponsor. Payouts of USD 263.5 million in 2025 were 114.79% of issuer-defined free cash flow of USD 229.6 million, the dividend continues in a year of negative free cash flow, and no holder of record is named in the supplied files. The board decides distributions, and the only brake found in the supplied files is the USD 100.0 million minimum availability that revolver-funded dividends require.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kgs-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 77; 10-K_2025-12-31_kgs-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 48; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C17

The fourth weakness is concentration: the four largest customers were about 30% of first-half revenue, 82.8% of compression assets are in two basins, and utilization of 98.2% leaves 1.82% of the fleet idle. A regional slowdown or the loss of one large customer reaches revenue quickly once units move to month-to-month terms terminable on 30 to 90 days' notice.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kgs-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_kgs-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 61; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_kgsq22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation C01

The fifth weakness is unproven and unquantified exposure. Power has one quarter of history and one disclosed lease, purchase commitments of USD 2.5 billion are binding, a Texas sales tax liability of USD 65.8 million is recorded and the Mexico payments matter has no estimated loss. Each can draw cash or delay deleveraging without adding earnings.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 30; Business & governance (CP-1A)

### Business profile and credit linkage

Kodiak Gas Services, Inc. provides large-horsepower contract compression in the United States, centred on the Permian Basin, and since April 1, 2026 has also leased distributed and behind-the-meter power generation after acquiring Distributed Power Solutions. The reporting entity is Kodiak Gas Services, Inc. on a consolidated basis; its senior notes are issued by the operating subsidiary Kodiak Gas Services, LLC and guaranteed by the parent and certain subsidiaries that the filings do not name, so every figure here is consolidated and there is no separate subsidiary perimeter to isolate.

Compression customers pay a fixed monthly fee, billed ahead of the service month and generally due within 30 days, for primary terms of one to seven years, or three to five years for large units, and most contracts carry an annual inflation adjustment. Compression was 84.4% of first-half 2026 revenue, power 4.5% and other services 11.1%. The structure resembles midstream take-or-pay: revenue depends on units staying under contract, not on gas volumes, which makes cash flow visible and sticky but ties it to renewals and to one product in one region. For creditors the model supports debt service and liquidity through each contract term, while refinancing confidence depends on how much of the fleet rolls onto new terms at similar rates and on whether the new power business earns what the capital spent on it requires.

Kodiak is a listed company on the New York Stock Exchange with no controlling holder named in the supplied files. Affiliates of EQT AB, which held about 43.1% at the start of 2025, sold their whole holding through secondary offerings and company repurchases by December 2, 2025, so there is no longer a sponsor either to extract cash or to support the company in stress. Financial policy has been to return cash and to grow together. Management states that it expects to fund dividends and budgeted growth spending from discretionary cash flow and, if that is short, from the revolver or by cutting growth spending. The revolver may fund a dividend only while pro forma availability stays at or above USD 100.0 million, and the note indentures limit distributions, investments, debt, liens and asset sales subject to exceptions, with most restrictions ending if two of three agencies rate the notes investment grade; no rating is supplied. ### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Compression revenue rose 7.4% in the second quarter of 2026 on 2.7% more revenue-generating horsepower and 4.1% more output per unit, with 5.3% fewer units, so growth comes from larger units placed under contract and has to be bought with growth capital. Management reports improving pricing and utilization, but the filings give no renewal pricing, and the rise in adjusted gross margin to 70.0% from 68.3% is the only evidence of price. Revenue is predictable and recurring inside a primary term, cyclical at renewal, concentrated in four customers and one region, and exposed to substitution because customers may buy their own compression or use other lift technology. Remaining contract revenue equals 2.07x to 2.11x a year of guided compression revenue, so visibility is a matter of years, not a decade, and the renewals of 2027 to 2029 set the cash flow that carries the 2031 maturities.

### Cost structure and margin resilience

Compression cost of operations was 29.97% of compression revenue in the second quarter of 2026 and selling and administrative costs were 10.46% of total revenue, which, with customers supplying fuel gas and reimbursing property and sales taxes, leaves an adjusted EBITDA margin of 55.4%. The filings do not split fixed from variable cost, so this analysis assumes that the labour, parts and maintenance of running a fleet do not fall quickly when a unit leaves contract, which is why the downside assumes that 70.0% of lost compression revenue falls through to adjusted gross margin. Margins can therefore be defended against input inflation inside contract terms but not against units leaving contract, and acquisition costs that run through selling and administrative expense add to the strain while the power business is integrated.

- Rivalry is regional and benign today: the filings describe numerous competitors able to adopt more aggressive pricing, but utilization of 98.2% and an adjusted gross margin of 70.0% show that rivalry is not eroding returns, and it would matter at renewal if rivals add fleet faster than demand grows.

- New entrants face capital and delivery barriers: management describes historically long lead times for new large-horsepower units, and Kodiak itself carries USD 2.5 billion of equipment orders, so entry is slow, although the annual report warns of entrants building newer and more flexible fleets.

- Substitutes are customer choices rather than technologies: customers may buy and run their own compression or choose another artificial-lift method, which would cut utilization directly, while electric motor drive is a conversion within the product.

- Buyer power is concentrated but offset by credit quality and contract form: four customers are about 30% of revenue and none is above 15%, they pay fixed fees and supply fuel, but after primary terms contracts end on 30 to 90 days' notice and a customer may terminate if the mechanical availability guarantee of 95.0% to 98.0% is missed.

- Supplier power is high: a small number of key vendors manufacture, package and assemble the equipment under no long-term contracts, so lead times and prices can rise and delay growth, although the company believes alternative sources are generally available.
### Macro, regulation and technology

Three factors matter to credit and one does not. Regulation and emissions standards favour modern large units, and electric motor drive is being deployed under long fixed-revenue contracts with select customers. Economic exposure runs through natural gas production, which management links to power-sector demand and exports, and through rates, where the issuer estimates that a 1.0% rise adds only about USD 3.1 million of revolver interest before swaps. Technology and customer demand for distributed power from data-center developers underpin the power strategy, which rests on management language until contracts are shown. Social factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver in the supplied materials.

### Credit-translated SWOT

Strengths that support credit are fixed-fee contracts with investment-grade customers, utilization of 98.2% at a 70.0% adjusted gross margin, liquidity of about USD 1.7 billion with no material maturity before 2030, and access to debt and equity markets. Weaknesses that constrain it are negative free cash flow in 2026, leverage of 4.52x reported EBITDA, payouts above free cash flow in 2025, and concentration in four customers and two basins.

Scale and competitive position are assessed as Average: four-quarter revenue of about USD 1.4 billion and a large fleet are meaningful, and tight equipment supply helps, but market share and peer data are not supplied. Business diversification is Weak, because compression is 84.4% of revenue, 82.8% of compression assets sit in two basins and the four largest customers are about 30% of revenue, while power is too new to diversify. Cost and capex flexibility is Average, since maintenance needs are low but USD 2.5 billion of orders are binding, and margin stability is Strong for compression, with adjusted gross margin of 70.0% and an EBITDA margin of 55.4%, tempered by thin other services.

### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next 12 to 24 months guidance points to adjusted EBITDA of USD 830 million to USD 860 million, up USD 80 million at the midpoint from the February guidance that excluded the acquisition but with growth and other capital spending USD 450 million to USD 490 million higher, which implies USD 423.1 million to USD 453.1 million in the second half against USD 406.9 million in the first, supported by contracted revenue covering 85.67% to 89.76% of guided second-half compression revenue and by the first deliveries of 61 megawatts of new power capacity in 2026. Headwinds in the period are the second-half cash call of USD 173.5 million to USD 283.5 million, working capital that has not reversed, integration of the power business and dividends of about USD 191.7 million; each presses on liquidity and leverage but not on any maturity.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-08-06_kgsq22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 7; EX-99.1_2026-05-11_kgsq12026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-02-25_kgsq42025earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 49; calculation C02; calculation C04; calculation C06; calculation C25

Over three to five years management targets more than two gigawatts of power capacity by the end of the decade, annual additions of several hundred megawatts through 2030 and a one-gigawatt turbine order for delivery by 2030. Sector tailwinds are rising demand for natural gas from the power sector and exports and tight equipment supply; sector headwinds are renewal repricing after the contract book rolls and rivals' fleet additions. Company-specific tailwinds are a contracted book that has grown 2.74x beyond 2026 and low maintenance needs; company-specific headwinds are power capital outlay running 3.20x to 4.74x the revenue guided for 2026 and a financial policy that keeps paying out. The medium-term credit outcome therefore turns on whether signed power contracts arrive before the equipment does.

### Downside scenario

The downside begins with a sustained fall in oil and gas prices that slows drilling and completions in the Permian Basin and Eagle Ford Shale, where 82.8% of compression assets sit. The first operational break is at renewal: units that have reached the end of their primary terms, 9.0% of horsepower at the end of 2025, can leave on 30 to 90 days' notice, and the contracted book thins quickly after 2027, so a loss of 10% of compression revenue is the illustrative size used here, about the whole month-to-month group and a little more. At the 70.0% adjusted gross margin the loss removes USD 85.5 million of EBITDA, so four-quarter adjusted EBITDA falls to USD 680.6 million and reported EBITDA to USD 517.9 million; total debt becomes 4.00x adjusted EBITDA and 5.26x reported EBITDA, and net debt 3.80x and 5.00x, while adjusted EBITDA still covers cash interest 3.68x and reported EBITDA 2.80x. If costs did not fall at all, the loss would be USD 122.1 million and total debt would be 4.23x adjusted and 5.66x reported EBITDA.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kgs-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_kgs-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 61; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C15

Interest costs do not fall in the scenario because 86.17% of principal is fixed-rate notes, and the dividend of about USD 198.2 million a year and the power build-out would keep drawing cash unless the board acts. Management's levers are to cut uncommitted growth orders, trim the dividend and slow power deliveries; the lever is limited near term by USD 587.9 million of commitments due within twelve months. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress, because liquidity of about USD 1.7 billion and no maturity before 2030 leave time, but the leverage covenant is the point where the scenario could bind and the lenders' definition is not supplied, so it cannot be sized. This is an illustrative sensitivity, not a forecast, and it assumes no new contracts offset the loss.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kgs-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-Q_2026-06-30_kgs-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 29; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_kgsq22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C06; calculation C12; calculation C15
### Overall credit view

Overall, Kodiak presents an adequate business profile supported by contracted, high-margin compression cash flows and a customer base of investment-grade names, but credit quality is constrained by negative free cash flow from a debt-assisted power build-out, leverage of 4.52x reported EBITDA and a financial policy that keeps paying out without a sponsor. Cash-flow durability appears adequate for compression and not fully assessable for power, which has one quarter of history. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on continued access to equity and notes markets, revolver availability, and renewals of the compression book from 2027 to 2029, with no maturity before 2030. The primary downside path is a fall in Permian demand that ends month-to-month units while power capital is already committed. Further analysis would require the lenders' covenant definitions, the proxy statement, power contract terms, the third-quarter results and current market prices. Top risk: debt-assisted power growth ahead of signed long contracts.

## Gaps

- The lenders' EBITDA, add-backs and cash netting behind the reported leverage of 3.2x are not supplied, so covenant headroom cannot be sized in EBITDA terms and the ratios computed here are not comparable with it; severity High; the compliance certificate would close it.

- The maintenance levels of 5.25x, 3.25x and 2.5x are printed only in the annual report, and the 2026 quarterly reports do not reprint them after the April 2026 amendment, so the levels in force at June 30, 2026 are not confirmed; severity High; the amended credit agreement would close it.

- The deduction of the 2031 note proceeds from debt in the leverage ratio applied only through June 30, 2026, so the reported ratio for later quarters follows different netting and the size of the effect is not stated; severity Medium; the third-quarter compliance certificate would close it.
- The borrowing base is not printed, so undrawn commitments of USD 1.6 billion are a ceiling and not confirmed availability; severity Medium; the borrowing base certificate would close it.

- Nothing dated after August 7, 2026 was supplied, so the second-half cash call, the year-end leverage indication and guidance may have changed; severity High; the third-quarter 2026 report would close it.

- Power contract terms other than one lease, pro forma earnings for the acquired business and the split of purchase commitments between compression and power are not disclosed, so power durability and the pace of capital calls are not established; severity Medium; later filings would close them.

- Financial foundation states pro forma net leverage on reported EBITDA only and no pro forma cash, so pro forma figures on adjusted EBITDA and for cash are not established; severity Low; a pro forma statement in a later filing would close it.

- No current bond prices, spreads, ratings or peer data were supplied, so market access and the standing of the business profile against other leveraged issuers are judged from the issues completed and not from a market read; severity Medium; market data would close it.
- The proxy statement was not supplied, so holders, board composition and pay are not established; severity Medium; the 2026 proxy statement would close it.

- The quarterly report's text and its cash flow statement disagree on the sign of the first-half 2025 working-capital movement (a use of USD 19.8 million in the text, a source of USD 19.8 million in the statement); the statement is used; severity Low; the issuer's correction would close it.

- The annual report describes a share repurchase program of up to USD 150.0 million, while the 2026 quarterly reports describe up to USD 100.0 million; both show USD 31.7 million remaining and the same expiry, and the remaining amount is used; severity Low; the board resolutions would close it.

- Business & governance locates the year-end remaining contract revenue one page later in the annual report than where the figures are printed; the amounts it states are correct, and this analysis cites the right page; severity Low; no change to any figure.
- No fleet valuation or recovery analysis is supplied or attempted here, so loss given default is not assessed in this fundamental view; severity Medium; the recovery analysis would close it.

- The guidance arithmetic uses issuer-defined free cash flow, which excludes working-capital movement and includes asset-sale proceeds, and assumes the fourth-quarter dividend equals the third, so the second-half cash call and the indicated year-end leverage are indications, not forecasts; severity Medium; the third-quarter report would close it.
